title: Solana LLM Oracle
summary: Ask an LLM from a Solana program: post a request on chain and receive the answer as a CPI callback signed by the oracle.
what: Solana LLM Oracle is an Anchor 0.31.1 program for on-chain AI requests. Requests and chat contexts are PDAs; an off-chain oracle answers by invoking the requester’s callback with a PDA signature.
app_note: The page at /dapps/solana-llm-oracle/ is the generic IDL-driven wallet console. The lab tree is branch sol-college-devnet of Blockchains/solana-llm-oracle, with declare_id changed and the admin and oracle identity set to the lab wallet.

try_steps.do: Open /dapps/solana-llm-oracle/, switch to Devnet, connect a wallet and call create_chat, then create_llm_inference with callback_program_id set to the program itself.
try_steps.see: A chat context and an inference request with is_processed = false.
try_steps.ran: The lab oracle answered with callback_from_llm (see steps).

diagram: user --create_chat(prompt)--> chat_context; user --create_llm_inference(question, callback)--> inference; oracle --callback_from_llm(answer)--> inference.is_processed + CPI callback(answer) signed by config PDA
innovation: The callback pattern lets any program consume AI output on chain and verify its origin through a PDA signature instead of trusting a transaction signer.
exercises: Why does callback_test check that the config account is a signer?
What could go wrong because callback_from_llm does not check the program account against the request?
